subject: SyncBound renewal: term convergence & staged onramp plan
messages:
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal coordination: term alignment & capacity for 2027

Hi Sofia / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here — we're trying to align multiple business units on a single renewal cadence and lock in the capacity uplift for our Q1 2027 campaigns. High level asks:

- Can we co-term the three active contracts into a single 24-month agreement that ramps capacity over the first 6 months?
- We want predictable unit economics during the ramp (ideally fixed token price bands per quarter).
- A short SOW that lists the phased capacity targets and an ops SLA would help our legal and ops teams.

Can you send a proposed structure and a short mutual action plan (timeline + signatures) by next Tuesday?

Attached a procurement intake (procurement@acme-retail.com) with our preferred billing cadence.

Thanks,
Tim Jenkins
Head of Procurement — Acme Retail
procurement@acme-retail.com

Attachments: intake-form-acme_2026.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: term alignment & capacity for 2027

Tim — thanks for the clear asks. We're able to support a consolidated 24-month term with a staged ramp. Outline below is our starting point; I'm attaching the cohort plan v2 and a SOW skeleton.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Term: 24 months, co-terming all three existing agreements into a single master contract.
- Ramp: Month 0-2: 40% of committed capacity (migration/onboarding), Month 3-6: linear ramp to 100%.
- Pricing: fixed token price bands per quarter for the first 8 quarters (we can set trigger-based true-ups if usage exceeds 110% of committed tokens).
- Ops: included SLA (uptime + latency P50/P95 targets) and quarterly performance reviews.

Requested next steps from Acme:
1) Confirm target signatories and billing entity.
2) Confirm whether you want monthly or quarterly invoicing (we can do quarterly in arrears or monthly prepay).
3) Approve the ramp percentages above or propose alternate cadence.

I'll loop Marissa for legal/sow cleanup once you confirm. We can have a draft mutual action plan by Monday.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_cohort-plan_v2.pdf; SOW-draft-Acme.docx
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: term alignment & capacity for 2027

Tim — following up with a slightly revised structure that smooths the billing and reduces your overruns during early months. Inline comments below.

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 09:15 Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tim — thanks for the clear asks. We're able to support a consolidated 24-month term with a staged ramp. Outline below is our starting point; I'm attaching the cohort plan v2 and a SOW skeleton.
> 
> Proposal summary (high level):
> - Term: 24 months, co-terming all three existing agreements into a single master contract.
> - Ramp: Month 0-2: 40% of committed capacity (migration/onboarding), Month 3-6: linear ramp to 100%.
> - Pricing: fixed token price bands per quarter for the first 8 quarters (we can set trigger-based true-ups if usage exceeds 110% of committed tokens).
> - Ops: included SLA (uptime + latency P50/P95 targets) and quarterly performance reviews.

Camila's adjustments / rationale:
- Ramp smoothing: propose Month 0-1: 30%, Month 2-4: step to 65%, Month 5-6: reach 100%. This avoids a big spike in months 2-3 when your campaigns go live.
- Billing: prefer quarterly invoicing with a built-in 8-week credit buffer in case of migration delays (reduces early overage risk).
- Pricing ladder: keep per-token bands but add a graduated discount at 150% usage to prevent punitive true-ups during promotional periods.

Attached is a short mutual action plan (draft) with milestones: technical kickoff, data migration window, pilot at 30% traffic, full ramp. We flagged the DocuSign flow in the file.

If this looks good, we'll:
- Produce a clean SOW (Marissa will own legal language).
- Generate the formal quote with the quarter-by-quarter token pricing.
- Draft the MxP (mutual action plan) and send to your signatories for DocuSign.

Would you be available for a 30-min alignment on Wednesday (Nov 3) to finalize signatories and billing entity?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Attachments: mutual-action-plan_syncbound.docx

Camila / Sofia — this looks reasonable and is a helpful framing for our legal and ops teams. Quick confirmations:

- Billing: quarterly invoicing is preferred.
- Ramp: we accept the smoothing cadence (30% -> 65% -> 100%).
- Signatories: I'll confirm the billing entity and signatories by EOD Tuesday.

Please proceed with the clean SOW and quote; we'll aim to have the DocuSign executed by Nov 18 to hit the Jan 1 kick-off.

Tim
